title: Root-normalized scalar extension of the first integral Tate line
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite-dimensional extensions of Q_l, and iota : E → L a Q_l-algebra embedding [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let S be a scheme on which l is invertible, with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let R_E and R_L be the completed integral coefficient ring sheaves and alpha : R_E → R_L the actual completed coefficient inclusion [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Write T_E and T_L for the first completed integral root lines, defined as the constant integer coefficient tensors with the common Z_l(1) root-limit module, endowed with their specified completed actions [def-pur-twist-sheaves]. Let beta be the constant ring-sheaf map induced by the integer inclusion. There is an isomorphism b : R_L tensor over R_E T_E → T_L such that, on every object U and all constant-integer-sheaf sections a and root-limit sections x, b(1 tensor (a tensor x)) = beta(a) tensor x. Moreover any alpha-semilinear module-sheaf map c : T_E → T_L satisfying c(a tensor x) = beta(a) tensor x equals the semilinear adjunct of b. No invertibility hypothesis is imposed on c. Tensor sections are the actual sheafification-unit images [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: The integral first line and its scalar-extension construction; elaboration of the first-line scalar-extension step of lem-route-twist-scalar-maps-exists-unique. Stacks sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict and section-tensor-product (03EK, 03EL).

proof.text: Compare the completed integer inclusion with the discrete integer inclusion after every finite quotient projection. The two constant-sheaf composites are equal by functoriality and the definition of the quotient inclusion. The limit projections give the discrete/completed square. The integer inclusion also commutes with the canonical Z_l inclusion, by their equalities in the coefficient fields. Consequently the two composites from the completed Z_l sheaf agree: after each finite target projection both factor through finite Z_l quotients, and finite-factor extensionality reduces their equality to the preceding constant square.

Reuse the proved canonical integralExtensionReverse isomorphism from the integral local-model module: completed scalar extension of the common root-limit module is the specified completed integral line. Its pure-tensor formula follows from integralExtensionReverse_section and the specified restriction of the completed action to discrete integers. The inverse equation used in the tower calculation follows from the isomorphism identities.

Extend the inverse source integral comparison by the ordinary tensor construction on morphisms (its two inverse equations are checked on pure tensors). Compose with the scalarExtensionTowerIso, transport along the completed coefficient-square equality, and compose with the target integral comparison. Every component is an isomorphism. The scalar-extension map formula, tower pure-tensor formula, transport formula and discrete/completed coefficient square give precisely b(1 tensor (a tensor x)) = beta(a) tensor x. No cover or finite local-model argument is needed again.

For uniqueness restrict the two completed-semilinear maps to the source discrete integer sheaf. The existing integralForgetIso identifies their source with its original sheafified tensor presentation. Cancel this isomorphism and use scalarExtension_hom_ext: equality on all displayed pure tensors implies equality of the restricted maps. Faithfulness of restriction gives equality of the original maps. Apply this to c and the scalar-extension embedding followed by b. This imposes no invertibility condition on c and makes no global lifting assertion about sheafified sections; it also covers the empty scheme and identity inclusion.

proof_origin.place: Integral first line; Stacks 03EK and 03EL, using the existing canonical integral scalar comparison and scalar-extension tower isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem firstRootCoefficientScalarComparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) L] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[Padic l] L) :
    let α := integralCompletedScalarMap l E L ι S
    let β : purTwistIntegralConstant S l E ⟶ purTwistIntegralConstant S l L :=
      (constantSheaf (ProEt.topology S) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (ULift.ringEquiv.symm.toRingHom.comp
          ((integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι).comp ULift.ringEquiv.toRingHom)))
    let res := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1}
      ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology S)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).map α)
    ∃ b : SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        α (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) ≅ purTwistIntegralModule S l L,
      (∀ (U : S.ProEtᵒᵖ) (a : (purTwistIntegralConstant S l E).obj.obj U)
        (x : (purTwistZlModule S l).val.obj U),
        b.hom.val.app U (SheafOfModules.scalarExtensionSection α
          (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) U 1 (purTwistIntegralTensor S l E U a x)) =
            purTwistIntegralTensor S l L U (β.hom.app U a) x) ∧
      ∀ c : purTwistIntegralModule S l E ⟶ res.obj (purTwistIntegralModule S l L),
        (∀ (U : S.ProEtᵒᵖ) (a : (purTwistIntegralConstant S l E).obj.obj U)
          (x : (purTwistZlModule S l).val.obj U),
          c.val.app U (purTwistIntegralTensor S l E U a x) =
            purTwistIntegralTensor S l L U (β.hom.app U a) x) →
        c = SheafOfModules.scalarExtensionEmbedding.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1} α
            (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) ≫
          res.map b.hom
